correctness.rationale: An exact binomial-neighborhood decomposition gives each joint weight and an adjacent-weight ratio verified against complete finite enumeration. The ratio lemma locates the conditional saddle and proves convergence; Chernoff/lower-bound arguments handle the extremely rare zone, and Laplace/Stirling analysis proves the critical LDP and probability phase boundaries. All assumptions, boundary values, and quantifiers appear in RESULT.md; finite experiments are supporting checks only.

value.rationale: Local girth at one root is a standard motivating criterion for tree-like exploration in G(n,p). Distinct n-dependent mechanisms cause a degree-one collapse, a Lambert saddle, a macroscopic critical suppression, and asymptotically ordinary degree; the further alpha=3/4 rarity boundary is structurally natural. Exact finite weights and a good conditional LDP are reusable, non-arbitrary probabilistic conclusions, not mere checker output.
